Same shape as exposure_in.json: code is the ticker (the desk prices it through the US watch feed), industry must match a cost/revenue industry string in commodities.json, commodities lists the board ids the name attaches to. Every number traces to the document in intensity_source. Built commodity by commodity from 2026-09-09; a name may carry `sides` {commodity id: cost|revenue} to override the industry's side on one card (an integrated steel maker: coking coal cost, iron ore revenue).

names.label: Southern Copper
names.intensity: Copper 74.8% of net sales in 2025 (net sales a record $13,420.0 million; average LME copper $4.51/lb, COMEX $4.82/lb). Company sensitivity for 2026: a $0.10/lb change in the copper price changes estimated annual net income attributable to SCC by $120.0 million (a $1.00/lb molybdenum move $34.8 million, $0.10/lb zinc $25.6 million, $1.00/oz silver $14.1 million), assuming expected production and sales, unchanged 2025 tax rates and no cost changes. The Q2 2026 10-Q restates it for the remaining six months of 2026: $59.6 million per $0.10/lb copper ($18.0 million per $1.00/lb molybdenum, $13.3 million per $0.10/lb zinc, $7.1 million per $1.00/oz silver). 2025 operating cash cost $2.17/lb before by-product credits and $0.58/lb net of by-products; H1 2026 net cash cost was a credit of $(0.03)/lb on higher silver and molybdenum by-product revenue
names.intensity_source: Southern Copper Form 10-K FY2025 (accession 0001104659-26-021492, filed 2026-02-27), Item 7 'Metal Prices' sensitivity table and 'Copper' market discussion; Form 10-Q Q2 2026 (accession 0001104659-26-089169, filed 2026-07-31), Item 2 'Metal Prices'
names.pricing_power: 10-K FY2025 Item 1: 'Prices for our products are principally a function of supply and demand and, with the exception of molybdenum, are established on COMEX and LME... From time to time, we have entered into hedging transactions to provide partial protection against future decreases in the market price of metals and we may do so under certain market conditions.' Item 7 Revenue Recognition: for certain copper and molybdenum sales, contracts allow pricing based on a month after shipment, 'in most cases within the following three months'; provisionally priced copper sales are marked to forward LME or COMEX prices each month until final settlement. 2025 net sales included $197.8 million of upward adjustments on provisionally priced sales
names.note: Sensitivity is stated on net income after tax, not EBITDA or revenue. Provisional pricing means part of a quarter's copper move settles through the next quarter's revenue. Revenues in US dollars; a significant part of costs is in Peruvian sol and Mexican pesos. Copper 74.8% of sales is the company's own figure; the remainder is molybdenum, silver, zinc and sulphuric acid by-products.

names.intensity_source: United Airlines Holdings Form 10-K for FY2025 (accession 0000100517-26-000023, filed 2026-02-12), Item 1 'Aircraft Fuel' table and Item 7A 'Aircraft Fuel'; Form 10-Q for Q2 2026 (accession 0000100517-26-000139, filed 2026-07-16), Item 2 operating statistics

Risk factors: 'If fuel prices were to then subsequently rise quickly, there may be a lag between the rise in fuel prices and any improvement of the revenue environment.'

names.label: Cameco
names.intensity: Uranium segment revenue C$2,874 million of consolidated revenue C$3,481.9 million in 2025, i.e. 82.5% (2,874 / 3,481.9); the rest is fuel services (conversion and fabrication), with the 49% Westinghouse stake equity-accounted. 2025 uranium average realized price US$65.53/lb (2024: US$58.45) against a UxC spot price of US$81.40/lb at 31 December 2025; 33.0 million lb delivered and 9.6 million lb purchased (including JV Inkai) in 2025. Company sensitivity for 2026: a US$5/lb rise in the uranium spot price adds C$36 million of revenue and C$8 million of adjusted net earnings but cuts cash flow by C$9 million (JV Inkai purchase entitlement of 4.4 million lb priced at a 5% discount to spot); a US$5/lb fall cuts revenue C$55 million, adjusted net earnings C$22 million and cash flow C$4 million. Expected realized price table at 31 December 2025 (US$/lb, spot scenarios $40/$60/$80/$100/$120/$140/$160): 2026 = 50/58/65/68/69/70/71; 2027 = 46/57/69/74/76/78/79; 2028 = 49/59/72/79/84/88/91; 2029 = 51/61/74/84 (higher scenarios continue). Long-term commitments of about 230 million lb after 2025 deliveries, averaging about 28 million lb a year over the next five years
names.intensity_source: Cameco 2025 annual MD&A dated 13 February 2026 (Exhibit 99.3 to Form 40-F, accession 0001193125-26-116229, filed 2026-03-19): 'Revenue, adjusted net earnings, and cash flow sensitivity analysis', 'Price sensitivity analysis: uranium segment', 2025 performance highlights and uranium segment results; Cameco 2025 consolidated financial statements (Exhibit 99.2 to the same 40-F), consolidated statement of earnings
names.lag: contract-lagged (company: 'changes to our average realized price will generally lag changes in market prices in both rising and falling price conditions'; delivery generally begins two years or more after signing; market-related prices are generally set a month or more before delivery)
names.pricing_power: MD&A 2025: 'We have a portfolio of long-term contracts, each bilaterally negotiated with customers, that have a mix of base-escalated pricing and market-related pricing mechanisms, including provisions that provide exposure to rising market prices while also protecting us when the market price is declining.' On the 2026 sensitivity: 'at the current price levels many of the market-related sales contracts we have delivered into or are delivering into this year are subject to ceiling prices and therefore are generally less sensitive than our purchase commitments.' Market-related contracts reference the spot or long-term price 'subject to specific terms unique to each contract, such as floors and ceilings set relative to market pricing at time of negotiation and typically escalated to time of delivery.' Fuel services is largely base-escalated. FX: US$1.01 billion of 2026 exposure hedged at 1.36 USDCAD
names.note: All money figures are Canadian dollars except uranium prices, which are US dollars. The 2026 upside is capped by ceiling prices in the contracts being delivered into; the lag given in the map is the company's own description. Cash flow moves against spot in the year of a JV Inkai purchase because the offsetting dividend arrives the following year. The 2029 realized-price row was cut off in the filing text extraction beyond the $100 scenario.

names.label: Alcoa
names.intensity: Company statement for 2025: 'energy comprised approximately 24 percent of the Company's total alumina refining production costs and electric power comprised approximately 24 percent of the Company's primary aluminum production costs'; Alcoa generated about 11% of the power its smelters used in 2025 and bought the rest, generally under long-term arrangements. Revenue mix 2025: Aluminum segment third-party sales $8,359 million (third-party aluminum $8,515 million less $156 million of energy sales and hedge results) and Alumina segment third-party sales $4,447 million (alumina $3,710 million plus bauxite $737 million) against consolidated sales of $12,831 million, so the Aluminum segment is about 65% of sales (8,359 / 12,831) and Alumina about 35%. No dollars-per-tonne LME or alumina price sensitivity is stated in the 10-K; Item 7A refers only to Note P (derivatives). Q2 2026: adjusted EBITDA $901 million, up $306 million sequentially 'primarily due to higher aluminum prices and shipments', partly offset by 'higher energy prices, primarily fuel oil and diesel increases associated with the Middle East conflict' and Section 232 tariff costs on Canadian metal
names.intensity_source: Alcoa Form 10-K FY2025 (accession 0001193125-26-077167, filed 2026-02-26), Item 1 'Energy Facilities and Sources' and 'Aluminum' pricing discussion, Item 7 segment tables (Alumina and Aluminum third-party sales) and Note E 'Sales'; Alcoa Q2 2026 results press release dated 16 July 2026 (Exhibit 99.1 to Form 8-K, accession 0001193125-26-306118)
names.pricing_power: 10-K FY2025 Item 1A: the price of primary aluminum is 'the underlying base metal component, which is typically based on quoted prices from the LME; (ii) the regional premium... associated with the physical delivery of metal to a particular region' plus a product premium; alumina is sold under contracts with 'the API price basis and a negotiated adjustment basis'. Energy: 'Pricing may be fixed, indexed to an underlying fuel source or other index such as LME, cost-based, or based on regional market pricing.' Note P: several power contracts are embedded derivatives that index the price of power to the LME price of aluminum (one also to the Midwest premium), so 'Increase in LME price and/or the Midwest premium results in a higher cost of power'. Q2 2026 release: Aluminum third-party revenue rose 31% sequentially 'partially offset by impacts from certain energy contracts linked to metal pricing'
names.note: Both figures are the company's own cost-share statements, not a per-$100/t sensitivity; Alcoa publishes per-tonne sensitivities only in its earnings slide decks, which were not in the filings opened. LME-linked power contracts (Brazil, Norway, Quebec) claw back part of an aluminum price rise through power cost. Natural gas exposure is concentrated in the Western Australia and Spain refineries; the 10-K gives no gas share separate from the 24% energy share of refining cost.

names.label: International Paper
names.industry: Integrated paper makers with own pulp
names.pricing_power: 10-K FY2025 Item 1A: 'We rely heavily on the use of certain raw materials (principally virgin wood fiber, recycled fiber, caustic soda, starch and adhesives), energy sources (principally biomass, natural gas, electricity and fuel oil) and third-party transport companies... we have not always been able to, and may in the future be unable to, recoup past or future increases in the costs of any raw materials, energy sources or transportation sources from customers... where we are able to recoup our cost increases, there may be a delay between the onset of the cost increases and the recoupment.' 'We have significant exposure to energy costs, in particular gas, electricity and other fuel costs... We have employed and expect to continue to employ, strategies, including hedging a portion of our energy costs.' Item 7A 'Commodity Price Risk': energy swaps and forward purchases had a net fair value of a $21 million liability at 31 December 2025 and 'the potential loss in fair value from a 10% adverse change in quoted commodity prices for these contracts would have been approximately $40 million'. Q4 2025 MD&A: EMEA 'input costs are expected to be higher primarily driven by elevated energy costs' in Q1 2026

IP is now a packaging company (DS Smith added in 2025; global cellulose fibers being divested), so 'own pulp' in the map label is integrated containerboard, not market pulp.

names.label: Chevron
names.intensity: Upstream earned $12,822 million of 2025 earnings against $3,022 million for Downstream and $(3,545) million for All Other, on net income of $12,299 million, so Upstream is more than 100% of the group result. Worldwide net oil-equivalent production 3.7 million barrels a day in 2025 (up 12% on Hess). Average sales prices 2025: crude $63.22/bbl consolidated ($62.25 in the US), NGL $18.91/bbl, natural gas $4.86 per Mcf worldwide but $2.04 in the US; TCO (Kazakhstan affiliate) crude $56.88. Average production cost $9.71 per barrel. No $/bbl earnings sensitivity is published in the 10-K

names.pricing_power: Own words, 10-K 2025 Financial and Derivative Instruments: "Chevron is exposed to market risks related to the price volatility of crude oil, refined products, NGLs, natural gas, LNG and refinery feedstocks. The company uses derivative commodity instruments to manage these exposures on a portion of its activity ... The results of these activities were not material to the company's financial position, results of operations or cash flows in 2025". 2026 production guided up 7-10% "assuming a Brent crude oil price of $60 per barrel"; about 21% of 2025 production was in OPEC+ countries where entitlement volumes move inversely with price
names.note: Integrated: Downstream (refining margins) partly offsets crude in a falling-price year, which is why the map keeps CVX on WTI/Brent/natgas_us but the integrated cushion is real ($3.0 billion Downstream in 2025 vs $1.7 billion in 2024 as crude fell). names.label: Occidental Petroleum
names.intensity: Company's own sensitivity for budgeted 2026: approximately $240 million of pre-tax cash for a $1 per barrel change in WTI and approximately $25 million for a $1 per barrel change in Brent; $0.50 per Mcf in domestic natural gas is about $120 million a year; a $0.25 change in the Midland-to-Gulf-Coast oil spread is about $55 million
names.intensity_source: Occidental Petroleum Form 10-K for fiscal 2025 (accession 0001628280-26-009059, filed 18 February 2026), Item 7A Quantitative and Qualitative Disclosures About Market Risk, Commodity Price Risk

These price-change sensitivities include the impact of PSC and similar contract volume changes on income. If production levels differ from the Company's 2026 budgeted production, the sensitivity of the Company's results to prices also will change." names.pricing_power: Own words, 10-K 2025: "Our 2026 cash flow is partly protected from commodity price volatility due to our current hedge position that covers approximately 30% of our anticipated oil and gas volumes. In order to further insulate our cash flow, we continue to examine and, when appropriate, execute attractive regional basis swap hedges"; and "if commodity prices decline further, we will adapt our plan by reducing activity in order to maximize free cash flow". Gas realized only 12% of Henry Hub before hedges in Q2 2026, a regional basis effect the 10-Q table shows but does not name

names.intensity_source: Schlumberger (SLB) Form 10-K for fiscal 2025 (accession 0001193125-26-021017, filed 23 January 2026), Item 7 2025 Executive Overview and Item 1A Risk Factors
names.pricing_power: Own words, 10-K 2025 Item 1A: "The oil and gas industry has historically experienced periodic downturns, which have been characterized by diminished demand for our products and services and downward pressure on the prices that we are able to charge. Sustained market uncertainty can also result in lower demand and pricing for our products and services"; Item 1: "customer budget constraints in North America may lead to lower demand for our services and products in the fourth quarter of the year". 2025 overview: "a challenging backdrop for the industry, with lower commodity prices, geopolitical uncertainty and an oversupplied oil market"

names.label: Valero Energy
names.intensity: Refining is the book: Refining segment revenues $116,166 million of $122,687 million total in 2025 (94.7%) with cost of materials and other $96,080 million, so the refining margin pool was $20,086 million (own arithmetic) on throughput of 2,988 thousand barrels a day; 1,090.6 million barrels a year means a $1 per barrel move in the crack is about $1.09 billion of pre-tax margin (own arithmetic, not a company figure). Company's own attribution for 2025 vs 2024: distillate margins +$1.8 billion, gasoline +$650 million, other products +$940 million, throughput +76,000 b/d worth +$340 million, crude differentials narrowing -$1.1 billion, other feedstock differentials -$600 million
names.intensity_source: Valero Energy Form 10-K for fiscal 2025 (accession 0001628280-26-011499, filed 25 February 2026), Item 7 Results of Operations (Refining segment margin bridge, throughput volumes) and Note on segment information (segment revenues and cost of materials); Item 7A Commodity Price Risk
names.pricing_power: Own words, 10-K 2025 Item 7A: "We are exposed to market risks related to the volatility in the price of feedstocks (primarily crude oil, waste and renewable feedstocks, and corn), the products we produce, and natural gas used in our operations"; derivatives are used only to manage LIFO inventory-level differences and favourable forward prices, and "the amount of gain or loss that would have resulted from a 10 percent increase or decrease in the underlying price for all of our commodity derivative instruments ... was not material". The margin is earned as a spread, so gasoline and diesel help and crude hurts, with no hedging of the crack itself
names.note: Valero publishes no crack-spread sensitivity; the $1.09 billion per $1/bbl is the reader's arithmetic on stated throughput. Renewable Diesel and Ethanol segments are small (revenues $4.6 billion and $5.0 billion) and 2025 carried a $1,131 million impairment on Benicia and Wilmington. Forward contracts on forecasted zinc and lead sales at 31 December 2025: 2026 settlements 53,407 thousand lb zinc at $1.33/lb and 42,108 thousand lb lead at $1.02/lb; 2027 settlements 23,810 thousand lb zinc at $1.36/lb; plus contracts on provisional sales. SA gold is partly hedged with zero-cost collars: an agreement from 2 December 2024 for 182,000 oz over 13 months (14,000 oz a month) with a floor of R45,000/oz and cap of R58,500/oz, and one from 2 January 2025 for 168,000 oz over 12 months with floor R45,000 and cap R54,400/oz; realised losses on the gold hedges were R1,288 million in 2025 and the fair-value loss R1,736 million as the rand gold price hit records. names.label: Solaris Energy Infrastructure
names.intensity: Two legs, and the power leg has taken over: Solaris Power Solutions revenue $333.5 million (54% of $622.2 million total) and 68% of segment adjusted EBITDA in 2025, 58% and 70% in Q4 2025, 72% of revenue and 80% of segment EBITDA in Q2 2026 (69% for H1 2026, total revenue $415.6 million); deployed power capacity about 630 MW in 2025 vs 230 MW in 2024.
